title: Two rings of cuts per handle keep one piece
claim: For every network of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts (positions embed the ring graph G cellularly in a closed orientable surface S of genus g): (1) after any set C of contacts is cut, the pieces read from which uncut contacts need which rings are exactly the components of G - C (every uncut contact needs both its rings from lag 1; needs follow walks of uncut contacts); (2) C leaves the network in one piece exactly when the cycle space of the cut contacts' dual edges injects into H1(S; Z2), so at most 2g independent rings of cuts keep one piece, some 2g do (tree-cotree), and more separate: two per handle; (3) on the torus a ring of cuts round it in each direction keeps one piece and a third separates; the genus-2 regular network of 16 rings with three contacts each (GL(2,3)) has every contact persistent at every lag at every size.
failure_conditions: A cut set whose native pieces differ from the components of the ring graph without the cut contacts.
A network and a cut carrying more than 2g independent rings of cuts that stays in one piece, or a tree-cotree system of 2g that separates.
foundation_claim_scope: Networks of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts on closed orientable surfaces; two-time knots only (A30); no distance.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's standing request on 2026-11-08.
